# Health

## Scope

Applies when the change touches clinical or patient data, medical devices. Not when the product holds no health data and is no medical device. Neighbours: `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`, `aidd-team:enterprise-controls`, `aidd-team:incident-response`.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2023-03-29 | A premarket submission for a cyber device includes the FD&C Act 524B items: the vulnerability monitoring plan, the cybersecurity processes, and an SBOM. | S5 |
| 2026-01-01 | USCDI v3 is the certification baseline for certified health IT (HTI-1). | S4 |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd assess`) | Clinical or patient data is privacy and compliance: major, the privacy and compliance pools, a DPIA or HIPAA risk analysis. | S1 |
| Specify | Minimum necessary data; access logging. FHIR resources and US Core profiles named, and the SMART App Launch scopes each client gets. The safety class for device software (IEC 62304). | S1, S2, S3, S7 |
| Specify | A certified API or a patient's access request is never blocked or slowed without an information blocking exception, recorded (45 CFR Part 171). | S4 |
| Implement | PHI encrypted in transit and at rest; an audit log for every access; no PHI in logs, fixtures, or prompts. The HIPAA Security Rule update is still proposed, so its controls are designed for, not claimed. | S1 |
| Implement | Device software: the IEC 81001-5-1 activities (threat model, secure coding, security tests). For a cyber device, also an SBOM per release and a vulnerability monitoring and disclosure plan (524B). | S6, S5 |
| Review | The hazard analysis (ISO 14971) is updated for the change; requirements trace to tests. | S8, S7 |
| Ship | Access-log anomalies and the error rate on clinical paths are rollback triggers; the incident reporting path is known. | S1 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FHIR validation | every produced resource validates against its profile | the HL7 FHIR validator (`validator_cli.jar`, 6.10.4) in the test commands | S2 |
| SMART scope tests | a token without a scope reads nothing that scope guards, and each US Core read returns only its profile's data | integration tests per scope and per profile against a test FHIR server | S3 |
| PHI scan | no PHI in logs, fixtures, or outputs | Presidio (`presidio-analyzer` 2.2.364) or an equivalent scanner | S1 |
| Access-control tests | each role sees only its records | tests per role and per record | S1 |
| Traceability check | every requirement has a test | requirements and their tests linked in StrictDoc (`uvx strictdoc==0.30.1 export .`, which fails on a link to a missing node), plus a check that every requirement links a test, for device software | S7 |

- From `aidd-team:enterprise-controls`: Dependency scan, Container scan and SBOM.
- From `aidd-team:threat-model`: Abuse-case tests.

## Owned elsewhere

- The HIPAA breach notification clock: `aidd-team:incident-response`.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/roles.json`. Steward: @thaithienvanid, who reviews every change to this pack's standards.
